data.title: Parametric Knowledge is Not All You Need: Toward Honest LLMs via Retrieval of Pretraining Data

summary.claim: LLMs become more honest when they decide whether to answer based on whether the answer exists in their pretraining data. RETAIN, which retrieves pretraining documents to judge answerability, beats R-Tuning by about 18 EM-F1 points.
summary.condition: Pythia-12b-deduped with its public Pile corpus; TIP-TriviaQA benchmark built from TriviaQA. Factual questions only.
summary.gap: (Authors) Tested only on a small model whose pretraining data is public (Pythia 12B); multi-hop and math questions are not covered.

data.title: Finding the Sweet Spot: Preference Data Construction for Scaling Preference Optimization

summary.claim: When scaling on-policy samples, picking the highest-reward response as chosen and the lowest as rejected makes performance drop. Picking the rejected response at μ−2σ of the reward distribution keeps improving performance as samples grow.
summary.condition: DPO preference data built by repeated sampling and scored by a reward model; four models, evaluated on AlpacaEval 2.
summary.gap: (Inferred) Only general instruction-following is evaluated, so it is unknown whether this selection rule helps safety alignment or calibration.

data.title: More is Less: The Pitfalls of Multi-Model Synthetic Preference Data in DPO Safety Alignment

summary.claim: DPO on synthetic preference data from multiple models raises general benchmark scores but also raises jailbreak attack success. Using only the target model's own responses is better for safety.
summary.condition: DPO safety alignment on Llama, Mistral and Qwen; worst when a stronger model (e.g., GPT-4o) gives the chosen response and the target model the rejected one.
summary.gap: (Inferred) It is not checked whether the proposed cause (high linear separability leading to shallow cues) also applies to other alignment methods such as PPO.

data.title: Restoring Calibration for Aligned Large Language Models

summary.claim: Preference alignment makes LLMs overconfident, partly through preference collapse. Calibration-aware fine-tuning restores calibration in the calibratable regime, and an EM-based ECE regularizer does so in the non-calibratable regime.
summary.condition: Preference-aligned LLMs further fine-tuned on domain knowledge; confidence measured from output probabilities.
summary.gap: (Inferred) Verbalized confidence and how confidence shifts under user pushback are not studied.

data.title: GuardReasoner-VL: Safeguarding VLMs via Reinforced Reasoning

summary.claim: GuardReasoner-VL, a VLM guard model trained with online RL to reason before it judges, beats the runner-up by 19.27% F1 on average.
summary.condition: 123K training samples over text, image and text-image inputs; SFT, then RL with rejection sampling, harder concatenated samples and a length-aware reward. 3B/7B released.
summary.gap: (Inferred) Video and audio inputs are not covered, and the types of moderation errors are not analyzed.

data.title: Seeing Through Deception: Misleading Creator Intent in Multimodal News

summary.claim: VLMs fail to infer a creator's misleading intent in multimodal news and rely on surface cues such as consistency and polished style. The DeceptionDecoded benchmark measures this.
summary.condition: 12K image-caption pairs tied to trustworthy reference articles; three tasks (intent detection, source attribution, intent inference); 14 VLMs evaluated.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The data is generated by a framework and may differ from real misinformation, though the authors report good transfer to real data.

data.title: ActiveDPO: Active Direct Preference Optimization for Sample-Efficient Alignment

summary.claim: ActiveDPO picks which preference comparisons to send for human labeling with a theoretically grounded criterion that works for non-linear rewards, aligning better with fewer labels.
summary.condition: The LLM being aligned defines the reward model used for selection; several models and real preference datasets.
summary.gap: (Inferred) Focused on general alignment quality; which samples get selected for safety-related preferences is not studied.

data.title: AlphaSteer: Learning Refusal Steering with Principled Null-Space Constraint

summary.claim: AlphaSteer learns refusal steering: a near-zero vector constrained to the null space for benign inputs and a refusal direction learned by linear regression for malicious inputs, improving safety without over-refusal.
summary.condition: Activation steering; several jailbreak attacks and general-utility benchmarks.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The benign/malicious split depends on the learned null space, so robustness to new attacks outside the training distribution is open.

data.title: LoX: Low-Rank Extrapolation Robustifies LLM Safety Against Fine-tuning

summary.claim: Fine-tuning breaks safety alignment, even on benign-looking data, because safety-critical low-rank subspaces are sensitive. LoX extrapolates this subspace further along its direction and cuts attack success by 11–54 points.
summary.condition: Training-free, applied to the weights of an aligned model; evaluated under benign and malicious fine-tuning attacks.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The abstract names no models or datasets, and whether the effect holds for large-scale fine-tuning is unknown.

data.title: Automating Steering for Safe Multimodal Large Language Models

summary.claim: AutoSteer uses an MLP probe on a layer chosen by a safety-awareness score to detect toxicity, and steers toward refusal only when toxicity is detected, sharply lowering multimodal attack success without retraining.
summary.condition: LLaVA-OV and Chameleon on VLSafe and ToViLaG+; VLSafe ASR on LLaVA-OV 60.0% → 4.2% with general performance kept.
summary.gap: (Authors) The probe may be weak on out-of-distribution attacks, only two models are tested, and ASR responds non-linearly to steering strength.

data.title: ConfTuner: Training Large Language Models to Express Their Confidence Verbally

summary.claim: ConfTuner fine-tunes with the tokenized Brier score, a proper scoring rule, so that an LLM's verbalized confidence matches its accuracy. It transfers to black-box models such as GPT-4o.
summary.condition: Diverse reasoning tasks, no ground-truth confidence labels needed; also helps self-correction and model cascades.
summary.gap: (Inferred) How confidence changes under user pushback, and whether internal confidence matches verbalized confidence, are not studied.

data.title: Alignment through Meta-Weighted Online Sampling

summary.claim: MetaAPO reduces the mismatch between offline preference data and the evolving policy: a meta-learner estimates where online sampling helps and gives per-sample weights. Online annotation cost drops by 42%.
summary.condition: Evaluated on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard and MT-Bench.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The abstract names no base models or datasets, and no effect on safety alignment is reported.

data.title: Attention Misses Visual Risk: Risk-Adaptive Steering for Multimodal Safety Alignment

summary.claim: MLLMs are vulnerable to harmful intent hidden in images partly because they pay too little attention to safety-critical image regions. MoRAS strengthens that attention, estimates risk, and adaptively steers toward refusal.
summary.condition: Inference-time defense with no extra generation and only a small calibration set; several MLLMs and benchmarks.
summary.gap: (Inferred) How representative the calibration set must be, and generalization to new kinds of multimodal jailbreaks, are open.

data.title: Angular Steering: Behavior Control via Rotation in Activation Space

summary.claim: Angular Steering rotates activations within a fixed 2D subspace, unifying vector addition and directional ablation in one geometric frame and giving smooth, fine-grained control of behavior.
summary.condition: Refusal and emotion steering across several model families and sizes; an adaptive variant rotates only activations aligned with the target direction.
summary.gap: (Inferred) How much rotation drags other behaviors (e.g., sycophancy, confidence) along is not studied.

data.title: Unlocking the Pre-Trained Model as a Dual-Alignment Calibrator for Post-Trained LLMs

summary.claim: Overconfidence in post-trained models comes from confidence drift (only final confidence rises) and process drift (intermediate inference paths diverge). Dual-Align, an unsupervised method, fixes both against the pretrained model.
summary.condition: Pairs of post-trained LLMs and their pretrained models; post-hoc correction that learns a single temperature parameter.
summary.gap: (Inferred) It needs the pretrained model, so it is hard to use when the pretrained checkpoint is not released.

data.title: The Facade of Truth: Uncovering and Mitigating LLM Susceptibility to Deceptive Evidence

summary.claim: LLMs filter obvious misinformation but are easily misled by polished, hard-to-falsify evidence: belief in false claims rises by 93% on average. DIS, which infers deceptive intent and warns early, reduces this.
summary.condition: MisBelief data: 4,800 instances made by role-playing LLMs, three difficulty levels; 7 LLMs evaluated.
summary.gap: (Inferred) Only generated evidence is tested, so the effect size on real human-crafted misinformation is unknown.

data.title: GuardReasoner-Omni: A Reasoning-based Multi-modal Guardrail

summary.claim: GuardReasoner-Omni, a guardrail model that reasons before judging, handles text, image, video and audio and beats prior state-of-the-art guards.
summary.condition: 181K training samples across four modalities; SFT cold start, then RL with a concise correctness reward. 3B/7B released.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The abstract names no benchmarks or baselines, and errors per modality are not analyzed.

data.title: BarrierSteer: LLM Safety via Learning Barrier Steering

summary.claim: BarrierSteer uses non-linear safety classifiers on hidden states as control barrier functions, pushing latent trajectories away from unsafe regions during generation and lowering attack success without changing weights.
summary.condition: Inference time; multiple safety constraints combined by constraint merging; several model families and datasets.
summary.gap: (Authors) The guarantees hold only if the learned barriers capture the intended safety property.

data.title: CompassDPO: Dynamics-Controlled DPO for Robust Safety Alignment

summary.claim: Noisy preference labels distort batch-level optimization. CompassDPO uses DPO's implicit reward margin to control update direction and size, giving stable safety alignment, especially under label noise.
summary.condition: PKU-SafeRLHF, four backbones, out-of-distribution safety benchmarks, label-flip noise; no external reward model.
summary.gap: (Inferred) Unreliable labels are judged only by the margin, so systematically biased labels (all wrong in the same direction) may still hurt.

data.title: Over-Refusal and Representation Subspaces

summary.claim: Over-refusal directions are task-dependent and high-dimensional, while harmful-refusal is a single task-agnostic direction. Ablating the global refusal direction reduces over-refusal only by accident and breaks the refusal mechanism, so task-specific geometric interventions are needed.
summary.condition: Geometry analysis and linear probing of hidden states in aligned language models; the two refusal types separate from early layers.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The abstract names no models or datasets, and it is unclear whether a task-specific intervention was built and tested.

data.title: How LLMs Are Persuaded: A Few Attention Heads, Rerouted

summary.claim: LLMs switch away from a correct answer under persuasion because of a few mid-layer decision heads: shallow heads read persuasive keywords and write an option-routing feature that redirects decision-head attention to the persuasion target.
summary.condition: Controlled multiple-choice tasks, four open-source model families, a GEO-based source-selection task; mitigated with a low-rank update to the decision heads' key projections.
summary.gap: (Inferred) Limited to multiple choice; whether the same circuit drives free-form answers or multi-turn user pushback is open.

data.title: V-DEAL: Diagnosing Video Safety De-Calibration as an Understanding-Refusal Coupling Failure

summary.claim: Video LLMs are more vulnerable when a harmful video comes with a benign question. They recognize the content over 81% of the time, but recognition is decoupled from refusal: visual understanding triggers a weaker refusal tendency than text.
summary.condition: Six Video LLMs, three public benchmarks; diagnosis at behavior, understanding and representation levels; prompt injection cuts ASR by 48.24 points on average.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The fix is a prompt injection; reconnecting understanding and refusal at the representation level is not addressed.

data.title: RISA: Response Inspection and Selective Actions for Refusal Calibration

summary.claim: RISA checks the initial response first and corrects refusal errors only when needed, improving refusal reliability without changing the base model and keeping most of its usefulness.
summary.condition: Rule-based scores combined with a calibrated linear probe on the prompt's final-layer hidden state; thresholds calibrated per base model.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The probe and thresholds must be recalibrated for each model, and the cost of probe errors is not given in the abstract.

data.title: The Mirage of Calibrated Confidence: Verbalized Confidence in Vision-Language Models

summary.claim: A VLM's verbalized confidence is largely independent of its reasoning: it can revise its reasoning, end up wrong, and still report high confidence. Calibration training can make this worse, and ECE and AUROC do not show it.
summary.condition: TGS-Bench with good/bad reasoning trajectory pairs over 10 benchmarks; TGS-self and TGS-pair metrics.
summary.gap: (Authors) Results are limited to the VLMs and calibration methods tested. (Inferred) Whether text LLMs or internal-representation confidence show the same gap is open.

data.title: Smaller Models, Better Rejects: Preference Distillation Scaling

summary.claim: In preference distillation, using responses from smaller frozen models as rejects beats the student's own failures: less compute and a stronger student.
summary.condition: Students from 7B to 72B, code generation and math reasoning; a DPO utility bound derived with a linearized feature model.
summary.gap: (Inferred) Only tasks with clear answers are tested, so it is unknown whether this holds for fuzzy preferences such as safety or honesty.

data.title: On the Algorithmic Bias of Aligning Large Language Models with RLHF

summary.claim: The KL regularization in standard RLHF distorts preferences and, in the extreme, causes preference collapse that nearly ignores minority preferences. PM RLHF fixes this by matching the response distribution to the preference distribution implied by the reward model.
summary.condition: Bradley-Terry-Luce/Plackett-Luce preference model assumed; OPT and Llama experiments, 29–41% better than standard RLHF.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The effect of preference matching on expressed confidence or calibration is not studied.

data.title: The Blessing and Curse of Dimensionality in Safety Alignment

summary.claim: High hidden dimensions help LLM performance but create linear structure in activation space that activation engineering can exploit to bypass safety alignment. Projecting representations to a lower dimension makes these jailbreaks less effective.
summary.condition: LLMs of several sizes, jailbreaks via representation engineering; theory linking hidden dimension and linear jailbreaks.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The abstract does not say whether reducing dimension also blocks general performance or useful steering.

data.title: POPS: Recovering Unlearned Multi-Modality Knowledge in MLLMs

summary.claim: Multimodal machine unlearning is not robust once a model is published. POPS optimizes a prompt suffix to make the model generate candidate private data and fine-tunes on it, recovering nearly all erased information.
summary.condition: An attacker with access to a published unlearned MLLM; several multimodal unlearning benchmarks.
summary.gap: (Inferred) Only the attack is proposed; no unlearning method that resists this recovery is given.

data.text: Images are an easier way to jailbreak AI than text.
data.basis: AI models often recognize a harmful image but still answer, and they pay less attention to the risky part of an image than to risky words. Nobody has compared the same harmful request sent as text and as an image on the same models.

data.text: More training data is not always safer.

history.text: More training data makes AI safer.
history.reason: More is Less showed that adding data from other models made jailbreaks easier.

data.basis: Several papers find that which examples go into preference training matters more than how many. The open question is when extra data starts to hurt safety.
